title: AQA GCSE English Language Paper 1: What Q2, Q3, Q4 and Q5 Actually Want
description: A concise student-friendly guide to the skills behind AQA English Language Paper 1 Questions 2, 3, 4 and 5, with practical answer checks.

children: AQA Paper 1 combines creative reading and writing. The fastest way to improve is to stop treating Questions 2, 3, 4 and 5 as four versions of the same task. Each rewards a different kind of thinking.
Q2: analyse language
Your job is to explain how specific words, phrases and language choices create meanings or effects. Do not simply identify a technique and move on.
A useful check before you move on
Have I selected a precise quotation?
Have I zoomed in on a meaningful word or phrase?
Have I explored an implication or connotation?
Have I connected the choice to an effect on the reader or presentation of the subject?
Q3: analyse structure

Structure is about how the text is organised and how its movements create the specific effect named in the question. Consider where the source begins, what it focuses on next, what changes and why the ending matters.
Look for
shifts in focus
changes of place or time
zooming in or out
introductions or withholding of information
contrasts
changes in pace
cyclical or contrasting endings
Q4: evaluate

This is a judgement question. Build a clear argument about how successfully the writer creates the effect or impression in the statement you are given. Evidence matters, but evaluation is more than spotting techniques.
A stronger response does three things
makes a clear judgement
selects evidence that genuinely supports that judgement
explains how the writer’s choices make the judgement convincing
Q5: creative writing

The writing task rewards controlled communication. A successful response does not need the wildest plot. It needs deliberate structure, accurate sentences, carefully chosen vocabulary and a clear sense of purpose.
Before writing
Decide on one central idea or mood.
For a story opening, plan the setting, character and a developing situation without rushing to resolve the whole plot. For description, plan deliberate changes in focus and atmosphere.
Choose two or three details you can describe precisely.
Vary sentence structures deliberately rather than randomly.
Before finishing
Check sentence boundaries.
Check commas and apostrophes.
Remove repeated vague vocabulary.
Make sure paragraphs are purposeful.
Check that your description has a deliberate final detail, or that your story opening ends at a point that creates expectation rather than completing the whole narrative.
The key distinction

Q2 asks how language creates meaning or effects. Q3 asks how organisation creates the named effect. Q4 asks you to evaluate the given statement. Q5 asks for controlled description or a story opening in response to the chosen prompt.
This guide is written to support the current AQA GCSE English Language 8700 course. Always use your school’s current materials and official AQA information for paper-specific instructions.
